title: Soupou Kandja with Palm Oil and Rice
author: Chimdindu Ken-Anaukwu
desc: A tomato-based okra stew in a cup of palm oil: onions and garlic, blended tomatoes, fish, shrimp or beef, finely chopped okra simmered to a silky body.
longDesc: The NKENNE printing is the simplified, tomato-forward kandia. A cup of palm oil is heated, onions and garlic cooked ‘until soft and fragrant’, blended tomatoes, hot peppers and seasonings cooked 8 to 10 minutes until slightly thickened, and fish, shrimp or beef added for 10 to 15 minutes. Finely chopped okra and water or stock then simmer 20 to 30 minutes until the okra turns silky, and the pot rests 5 to 10 minutes off the heat. It is the only kandia source here that builds on blended tomatoes.
ingredients: 1 to 1.5 pounds fresh okra, chopped finely
1 cup palm oil (or red palm oil)
1 to 2 pounds protein: fish (such as tilapia or snapper), shrimp, or beef
1 to 2 Scotch bonnet or hot peppers, adjust for heat
Salt, black pepper, dried shrimp or crayfish powder, bay leaves, thyme — quantities not printed
steps: Heat the palm oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onions and garlic and cook until soft and fragrant.
Add the blended tomatoes, hot peppers and seasonings. Cook 8 to 10 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the fish, shrimp or meat, stir gently, and cook 10 to 15 minutes to infuse the flavours.
Add the finely chopped okra and enough water or stock to reach the consistency you want. Reduce the heat and simmer 20 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally; the okra thickens to a silky texture.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Let the stew rest off the heat 5 to 10 minutes.
chefTips: ‘Until soft and fragrant’ and ‘until the sauce thickens slightly’ are the two printed cues.
The page says the stew often tastes better the next day.
Chop the okra very fine; larger pieces give a stringier texture.
This is a one-cup palm-oil stew. Cut back if you want it lighter — the page does not.
commonMistakes: Skipping the rest off the heat.
Adding all the liquid at once — add as needed for the consistency you want.
reheating: Low heat with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Tomato gives lycopene; fish or shrimp give lean protein.
A full cup of palm oil is rich in saturated fat; serve in moderation.
culturalNote: The page ties the dish to Wolof resourcefulness — affordable local ingredients, a large shared bowl, and the Wolof idea of teranga, hospitality. The author writes from a Nigerian food blog, NKENNE, and the dish’s Senegalese framing is hers.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Soupou Kandja (Kandia Soup): Silky Okra Stew with Palm Oil and Rice’. Byline: ‘Written By Chimdindu Ken-Anaukwu’, repeated as ‘By: Chimdindu Ken-Anaukwu’. Site: NKENNE. DATE: ‘Jul 18’ — NO YEAR PRINTED, flagged. Yield: ‘For 6 servings’. TWO-PASS, fully literal on both passes.
Total time on the page: about 50 to 70 minutes. The prep/rest/cook split here is the sum of the stated step times.
NOTE: no Wolof orthography is labelled on the page; it says only ‘Deeply rooted in Wolof traditions’.
DIVERGENCE, recorded not reconciled: the only kandia source in this set built on blended tomatoes. SEN029 uses 1 tbsp tomato concentrate; SEN028 and SEN031 use none.
ABSENT, not estimated: quantities of the seasonings (salt, black pepper, dried shrimp or crayfish powder, bay leaves, thyme).
